LESSON: READING FLUENCY: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading 2.2 Reading Fluency (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building- extended family 
Topic 2.4: Reading Fluency: Pronunciation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading Fluency: Pronunciation, part of Reading 2.2 Reading Fluency (2 sessions) • Vocabulary building- extended family  in Grade 9 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How can you improve your pace when reading Arabic?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read simple words with the correct pronunciation of particles (har

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Fluency: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Fluency: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply appropriate speed when reading a text for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Fluency: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. develop an interest in reading Arabic texts.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading Fluency: Pronunciation in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

A. read simple words with the correct pronunciation of particles (har

   Reading Fluency: Pronunciation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. develop an interest in reading Arabic texts.

   Reading Fluency: Pronunciation helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. engage in reading short sentences on routine and schedules,

2. identify vocabulary and phrases related to the theme,

3. work jointly to read the identified words while focusing on the correct pronunciation of particles (harf),

4. apply appropriate speed for fluency,

5. read a text of their interest independently during free time.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. engage in reading short sentences on routine and schedules,
2. identify vocabulary and phrases related to the theme,
3. work jointly to read the identified words while focusing on the correct pronunciation of particles (harf),
4. apply appropriate speed for fluency,
5. read a text of their interest independently during free time.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading Fluency: Pronunciation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: This is enhanced as the learner builds on their own learning experience when reading texts of their

interest independently during free time.

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is nurtured as the learner follows simple instructions to apply appropriate speed

for fluency.
